title: model-router: Haiku tier, effort caps and feedback loop
lead: A fork of a Claude Code plugin that picks a model for each subagent. This plan sends mechanical work to Haiku, caps reasoning effort per tier, shows main-conversation cost and tunes itself from outcomes.
what_you_do: Judge the nine criteria below. Seven (A1-A7) you can judge now on the README and the two sample pages. A8 and A9 are not yet demonstrable: A8 needs the first accepted weekly decision (after 2026-11-09) and A9 needs a new session with the router loaded. Answer Q5 only if you want to change the default.
north_star: Subagent work runs on the cheapest model and effort that is safe, and the rules improve from real outcomes.
thesis: Effort is the cheaper lever than a second model; Haiku is safe only where a cheap check exists; outcomes show loud failures but not silent ones.
disproof: If simple-tier runs show a bad-outcome rate above the weekly review's raise threshold (12%), the Haiku tier is too wide.
not_for: Changing the main conversation's model, which a plugin cannot do.
